claims.text: An MTP-based perturbation scheme will reduce computational cost by 10-100x relative to standard thermodynamic integration.
The MTP-based scheme will maintain free-energy accuracy within 5 meV/atom.
Including disordered liquid structures in the MTP training set will avoid extrapolation errors.
Experimental melting-property measurements for the Ta-based refractory HEA are infeasible.
Ab initio free-energy calculations for this alloy are prohibitively expensive.
A liquid-trained MTP perturbation scheme can estimate the solid-liquid free-energy difference without full thermodynamic integration over the phase space.
The multi-component liquid has a complex structure.
The MTP moment-tensor descriptors can represent the relevant disordered liquid local environments.
EAM potentials fail to capture the disordered liquid structure adequately.
Interpolation by the MTP permits efficient sampling of liquid-phase free energy through perturbation.
The perturbation scheme avoids expensive sampling of the solid phase.
The perturbation scheme avoids the full integration path required by ab initio methods.
Moment-tensor descriptors ensure transferability to a complex multi-component liquid.
The scheme will predict melting temperature with accuracy comparable to ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The scheme will predict the solid-liquid free-energy difference with accuracy comparable to ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The reduced computational cost will enable high-throughput screening of Ta-based HEAs.
The method may fail when the liquid structure lies substantially outside the MTP training distribution.
The method may fail when strong chemical ordering is not represented by the potential.
The MTP scheme is falsified if its melting-temperature prediction differs by more than 5% from the ab initio reference.
The claimed efficiency gain is falsified if the computational-time reduction is less than 10x at matched accuracy.

contradictions.description: The MTP is specified as trained exclusively on liquid configurations and the mechanism says expensive solid-phase sampling is avoided, yet the method is claimed to predict a solid-liquid free-energy difference. No solid-phase model, reference free energy, or perturbative connection for the solid is specified, creating an internal methodological inconsistency.
